1	# Jotter: the notyours demo app
2	
3	Jotter is a small notes app that notyours tests in the demo video.
4	
5	**These bugs are seeded and labelled on purpose.** Jotter contains three authorization mistakes of
6	the kind coding agents often ship, so notyours has something real to find. Each one is marked in the
7	code with a `// SEEDED BUG #n` comment and pinned by a test. Everything else is meant to be correct,
8	including guest access. Don't copy this code into a real app, and don't expose it to a network. The
9	server only listens on `127.0.0.1`.
10	
11	## Run it
12	
13	```bash
14	node demo/server.js --seed      # reset the database to the fixed seed, then serve http://127.0.0.1:3077
15	node demo/server.js             # keep existing data (seeds automatically if the database is empty)
16	node demo/server.js --seed-only # reset and exit
17	```
18	
19	Options: `--port <n>` (default 3077, or `$PORT`) and `--db <file>` (default `demo/data/jotter.sqlite`,
20	gitignored). The stack is Express 5, server-rendered HTML and sql.js (SQLite in WASM, no native modules).
21	
22	## Seed
23	
24	Re-seeding always produces the same users, note ids and URLs, so cached (0-credit) Kane replays
25	keep working.
26	
27	| User | Plan | Password (dev default) | Seeded data |
28	|---|---|---|---|
29	| `alice@jotter.test` | Pro | `alice-jotter-dev`, or `$JOTTER_ALICE_PW` | note **1001** "Travel documents": `Passport no. <alice token>` |
30	| `bob@jotter.test` | Free | `bob-jotter-dev`, or `$JOTTER_BOB_PW` | note **1002** "Reminder": `<bob token>`; his `/account` bio also shows `<bob token>` |
31	
32	New sign-ups are free users, and their notes start at id 1003.
33	
34	**Canary tokens** are read from the first `identities.json` that exists: `$NOTYOURS_DIR/identities.json`,
35	then `demo/.notyours/identities.json`, then `./.notyours/identities.json`. The file may be an
36	`Identity[]` array or an object keyed by id. Only `token` is read, and invalid tokens are ignored.
37	Without a file the fixed defaults are `NY-ALICE-JOTTERSEED2A` and `NY-BOB-JOTTERSEED2B`. Passwords
38	come only from the environment variables above, set when you seed. Re-seed after changing tokens or
39	passwords.
40	
41	## Pages and API
42	
43	| Route | What it does |
44	|---|---|
45	| `/signup`, `/login`, `/logout` | Account basics (`/logout` takes GET or POST) |
46	| `/notes` | Your own notes (correctly scoped) |
47	| `/notes/new` | Write a note |
48	| `/notes/:id` | View a note (**SEEDED BUG #1**) |
49	| `/account` | Plan and profile bio, with bio editing (correctly scoped) |
50	| `/pro/export` | Export page: Pro users see an "Export my notes" button, free users see an upsell |
51	| `GET /api/notes/:id` | Note as JSON (**SEEDED BUG #2**) |
52	| `POST /api/export` | Your notes as `jotter-export.txt` (**SEEDED BUG #3**). Other methods get `405` with `Allow: POST` |
53	
54	## The seeded bugs
55	
56	| # | Where | Mistake | What a correct app does |
57	|---|---|---|---|
58	| 1 | `routes/notes.js`, `GET /notes/:id` | Loads the note by id only, so any logged-in user can read anyone's note. | Adds `AND owner_id = <me>` and returns 404 |
59	| 2 | `routes/notes.js`, `GET /api/notes/:id` | Returns the full record, including owner email and body, for any id. | Same owner check |
60	| 3 | `routes/pro.js`, `POST /api/export` | The Pro gate is only a hidden button. The endpoint checks login, never the plan. | Returns 403 unless `plan = 'pro'` |
61	
62	**What stays correct (the controls):** guests get a redirect to `/login` from every page and a
63	`401` from every API route. `/notes` and `/account` only show your own data. So the guest boundary
64	holds, which shows that notyours doesn't cry wolf.
65	
66	## notyours boundaries (`demo/.notyours/`)
67	
68	`config.yaml` sets `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:3077`. Paths in `surface` are relative to `demo/`.
69	
70	| File | Kind | Viewer → target | Expected on this app |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| `b1-cross-user.yaml` | cross-user | Bob → `/notes/1001`, `/api/notes/1001` | **LEAK** (bugs #1, #2) |
73	| `b2-guest.yaml` | guest | logged out → same URLs | **HELD** |
74	| `b3-plan-gate.yaml` | plan-gate | free Bob → `/pro/export`; `POST /api/export` | **LEAK** via the API (bug #3); the UI path holds |
75	| `b4-sweep.yaml` | sweep | Bob → his own `/notes`, `/account` | **HELD** (Bob's token present, Alice's absent) |
76	
77	In B3, `targets.api` is written as `"POST <url>"` because the export endpoint only accepts POST. A GET returns `405` (with `Allow: POST`), never a 404, so a wrong-method probe is visibly wrong and not a "denied".
78	
79	## Tests
80	
81	```bash
82	npx vitest run --root demo
83	```
84	
85	These are real HTTP requests against an in-memory database, with no Kane. They check that bugs #1–#3
86	are present, guests are blocked, positive controls work (owners see their own tokens), the happy
87	paths work, and every boundary file parses with `BoundarySchema.strict()`.
88

# Jotter: the notyours demo app

Jotter is a small notes app that notyours tests in the demo video.

**These bugs are seeded and labelled on purpose.** Jotter contains three authorization mistakes of
the kind coding agents often ship, so notyours has something real to find. Each one is marked in the
code with a `// SEEDED BUG #n` comment and pinned by a test. Everything else is meant to be correct,
including guest access. Don't copy this code into a real app, and don't expose it to a network. The
server only listens on `127.0.0.1`.

## Run it

```bash
node demo/server.js --seed      # reset the database to the fixed seed, then serve http://127.0.0.1:3077
node demo/server.js             # keep existing data (seeds automatically if the database is empty)
node demo/server.js --seed-only # reset and exit
```

Options: `--port <n>` (default 3077, or `$PORT`) and `--db <file>` (default `demo/data/jotter.sqlite`,
gitignored). The stack is Express 5, server-rendered HTML and sql.js (SQLite in WASM, no native modules).

## Seed

Re-seeding always produces the same users, note ids and URLs, so cached (0-credit) Kane replays
keep working.

| User | Plan | Password (dev default) | Seeded data |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alice@jotter.test` | Pro | `alice-jotter-dev`, or `$JOTTER_ALICE_PW` | note **1001** "Travel documents": `Passport no. <alice token>` |
| `bob@jotter.test` | Free | `bob-jotter-dev`, or `$JOTTER_BOB_PW` | note **1002** "Reminder": `<bob token>`; his `/account` bio also shows `<bob token>` |

New sign-ups are free users, and their notes start at id 1003.

**Canary tokens** are read from the first `identities.json` that exists: `$NOTYOURS_DIR/identities.json`,
then `demo/.notyours/identities.json`, then `./.notyours/identities.json`. The file may be an
`Identity[]` array or an object keyed by id. Only `token` is read, and invalid tokens are ignored.
Without a file the fixed defaults are `NY-ALICE-JOTTERSEED2A` and `NY-BOB-JOTTERSEED2B`. Passwords
come only from the environment variables above, set when you seed. Re-seed after changing tokens or
passwords.

## Pages and API

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/signup`, `/login`, `/logout` | Account basics (`/logout` takes GET or POST) |
| `/notes` | Your own notes (correctly scoped) |
| `/notes/new` | Write a note |
| `/notes/:id` | View a note (**SEEDED BUG #1**) |
| `/account` | Plan and profile bio, with bio editing (correctly scoped) |
| `/pro/export` | Export page: Pro users see an "Export my notes" button, free users see an upsell |
| `GET /api/notes/:id` | Note as JSON (**SEEDED BUG #2**) |
| `POST /api/export` | Your notes as `jotter-export.txt` (**SEEDED BUG #3**). Other methods get `405` with `Allow: POST` |

## The seeded bugs

| # | Where | Mistake | What a correct app does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `routes/notes.js`, `GET /notes/:id` | Loads the note by id only, so any logged-in user can read anyone's note. | Adds `AND owner_id = <me>` and returns 404 |
| 2 | `routes/notes.js`, `GET /api/notes/:id` | Returns the full record, including owner email and body, for any id. | Same owner check |
| 3 | `routes/pro.js`, `POST /api/export` | The Pro gate is only a hidden button. The endpoint checks login, never the plan. | Returns 403 unless `plan = 'pro'` |

**What stays correct (the controls):** guests get a redirect to `/login` from every page and a
`401` from every API route. `/notes` and `/account` only show your own data. So the guest boundary
holds, which shows that notyours doesn't cry wolf.

## notyours boundaries (`demo/.notyours/`)

`config.yaml` sets `baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:3077`. Paths in `surface` are relative to `demo/`.

| File | Kind | Viewer → target | Expected on this app |
|---|---|---|---|
| `b1-cross-user.yaml` | cross-user | Bob → `/notes/1001`, `/api/notes/1001` | **LEAK** (bugs #1, #2) |
| `b2-guest.yaml` | guest | logged out → same URLs | **HELD** |
| `b3-plan-gate.yaml` | plan-gate | free Bob → `/pro/export`; `POST /api/export` | **LEAK** via the API (bug #3); the UI path holds |
| `b4-sweep.yaml` | sweep | Bob → his own `/notes`, `/account` | **HELD** (Bob's token present, Alice's absent) |

In B3, `targets.api` is written as `"POST <url>"` because the export endpoint only accepts POST. A GET returns `405` (with `Allow: POST`), never a 404, so a wrong-method probe is visibly wrong and not a "denied".

```bash
npx vitest run --root demo
```

These are real HTTP requests against an in-memory database, with no Kane. They check that bugs #1–#3
are present, guests are blocked, positive controls work (owners see their own tokens), the happy
paths work, and every boundary file parses with `BoundarySchema.strict()`.

There's now a **Duplicate note** button on the note page. It makes a copy titled "Copy of …" and takes you to the new note.

**What changed**
- **Button** (`routes/notes.js:70`): it sits at the top right of the note page, across from "← My notes". It's a small POST form styled like the app's other buttons, and only the note's owner sees it.
- **Route** `POST /notes/:id/duplicate` (`routes/notes.js:86`):
  - It only finds the note if it belongs to you, so someone else's note id gets a 404 and never a copy.
  - Guests are sent to `/login`, like every other page.
  - The copy keeps the body exactly as it was, gets a new creation date, and has its title cut to the app's 200-character limit.

**The security catch:** because of seeded bug #1, Bob can still open Alice's note 1001. Without the owner check, the new route would have let him copy her note, passport token included, into his own account, and it would then show up in his notes list. That would be a fourth leak, and an unlabelled one. The tests pin this down: Bob sees no button on her note, his POST gets a 404, and his notes list never shows her token. I left the three seeded bugs alone.

**Tests:** I added four tests to `test/jotter.test.js`: copying your own note, the title length limit, Bob being blocked, and guests and bad ids. All 22 tests in that file pass. `test/boundaries.test.js` can't run because it imports `../../src/schemas.ts`, which is outside this repo. It fails the same way without my change.

content.text:
I fixed the leak the notyours hook reported. Bob can no longer read Alice's note, but two of the repo's own tests now fail, because they check that these bugs exist.

**What I changed** (`routes/notes.js`): `GET /notes/:id` and `GET /api/notes/:id` now only find a note if it belongs to the logged-in user, which is the same check the new duplicate route uses. Another user's note id now gets a 404, just like a missing note. These were seeded bugs #1 and #2, which were there before the duplicate button. I updated the code comments that described them as present.

**Checked on the live server** (port 3077, restarted at 19:41:04, after my edit), logged in as Bob:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `/notes/1001`, `/api/notes/1001` (Alice's) | 404 |
| `/notes/1002`, `/api/notes/1002` (Bob's own) | 200 |
| `POST /notes/1001/duplicate` | 404 |

**The trade-off:** the README calls these bugs deliberate, there for the notyours demo. So fixing them changes what the demo app is meant to show:
- In `test/jotter.test.js`, the two "seeded bugs are present" tests for #1 and #2 now fail. The other 20 pass. I didn't edit any tests, as the hook told me.
- The README still lists bugs #1 and #2 as present, and says boundary b1 is expected to leak. Both are now out of date.
- One comment in my duplicate test now has the wrong reason. It says Bob can read `/notes/1001` "only because of SEEDED BUG #1", but that page is now a 404. The test still passes.

If you want the demo app back as it was, revert the two lookups (reverting the whole file would also remove the duplicate route, which has its own owner check, so the feature doesn't depend on them). Otherwise I can update the README and those two tests to match the fix.

Bug #3 (`POST /api/export` doesn't check the plan) is still there. The hook hasn't reported it, so I left it alone. Nothing is committed.
